children.description: The Laysan finch (Telespiza cantans), sometimes referred to by its Hawaiian name, ʻekupuʻu, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper, that is endemic to the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands.

children.name: Telespiza ultima
children.description: The Nīhoa finch (Telespiza ultima) is one of the two endemic bird species of the tiny Hawaiian island of Nīhoa, the other being the Nīhoa millerbird..

children.name: Palmeria
children.description: The Akohekohe — one of the most spectacular Hawaiian honeycreepers, with an extraordinary crest and vivid orange-red plumage patches.

children.name: Palmeria dolei
children.description: The ʻākohekohe, or crested honeycreeper, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper. It is endemic to the island of Maui in Hawaiʻi. The ʻākohekohe is susceptible to mosquito‐transmitted avian malaria and only breeds in high‐elevation wet forests.

children.name: Pseudonestor
children.description: The Maui Parrotbill — a critically endangered Hawaiian honeycreeper with a massively powerful, parrot-like bill for tearing apart wood to find beetle larvae.

children.name: Pseudonestor xanthophrys
children.description: The kiwikiu or Maui parrotbill (Pseudonestor xanthophrys) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Maui in Hawaii.

children.name: Melamprosops
children.description: The Poo-uli — discovered in 1973, extinct by 2004. It represented a unique evolutionary lineage with no close relatives among known Hawaiian birds.

children.name: Melamprosops phaeosoma
children.description: The poʻo-uli (Melamprosops phaeosoma)  or  Hawaiian black-faced honeycreeper is an extinct species of passerine bird that was endemic to the island of Maui in Hawaiʻi..

children.name: Oreomystis
children.description: The Akikiki — a tiny bark-creeping honeycreeper confined to Kauai's native forest, now one of the most critically endangered birds in the world.

children.name: Oreomystis bairdi
children.description: The ʻakikiki (pronounced ) (Oreomystis bairdi), also called the Kauaʻi creeper, is a critically endangered Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to Kauaʻi, Hawaiʻi..

children.name: Paroreomyza
children.description: Hawaiian creepers — small bark-foraging honeycreepers, several species of which are now extinct due to introduced rats and avian disease.

children.name: Paroreomyza maculata
children.description: The Oʻahu ʻalauahio (Paroreomyza maculata), also known as the Oʻahu creeper, is a small finch-like Hawaiian honeycreeper that is endemic to the Hawaiian island of Oahu..

children.name: Paroreomyza flammea
children.description: The kākāwahie or Molokaʻi creeper (Paroreomyza flammea) is an extinct species of Hawaiian honeycreeper..

children.name: Magumma
children.description: The Anianiau — the smallest Hawaiian honeycreeper and one of the few with a relatively stable population, confined to Kauai's native forest.

children.name: Magumma parva
children.description: The ʻanianiau (pronounced ) (Magumma parva) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper that is endemic to upper elevation forests on the island of Kauai..

children.name: Chloridops
children.description: The Kona Grosbeak — an extinct Hawaiian honeycreeper with an enormously massive bill for crushing the hard seeds of the naio tree, last seen in 1894.

children.name: Chloridops kona
children.description: The Kona grosbeak (Chloridops kona) is an extinct species of Hawaiian honeycreeper.

children.name: Rhodacanthis
children.description: Koa finches — extinct Hawaiian honeycreepers with large bills adapted for crushing native koa pods, eliminated by introduced rats and forest clearance in the 19th century.

children.name: Rhodacanthis flaviceps
children.description: The lesser koa finch (Rhodacanthis flaviceps) is an extinct species of Hawaiian honeycreeper in the subfamily Carduelinae of the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Rhodacanthis palmeri
children.description: The greater koa finch (Rhodacanthis palmeri) is an extinct species of Hawaiian honeycreeper in the subfamily Carduelinae of the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Loxioides
children.description: The Palila — a critically endangered Hawaiian honeycreeper entirely dependent on the mamane tree, and the subject of landmark environmental law cases in the USA.

children.name: Loxioides bailleui
children.description: The palila (Loxioides bailleui) is a critically endangered finch-billed species of Hawaiian honeycreeper..

children.name: Chlorodrepanis
children.description: Hawaiian amakihis — adaptable honeycreepers showing documented genetic resistance to avian malaria, allowing recolonisation of lower elevations than other honeycreepers can survive.

children.name: Chlorodrepanis virens
children.description: The Hawaiʻi ʻamakihi (Chlorodrepanis virens), also known as the common ʻamakihi, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper..

children.name: Chlorodrepanis flava
children.description: The Oʻahu ʻamakihi (Chlorodrepanis flava) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Chlorodrepanis stejnegeri
children.description: The Kauaʻi ʻamakihi (Chlorodrepanis stejnegeri) is a species of Hawaiian honeycreepers endemic to Kauaʻi in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Rhodospiza
children.description: The Desert Finch — a distinctive pale finch of Central Asian and Middle Eastern arid zones; the sole member of its genus.

children.name: Rhodospiza obsoleta
children.description: thumb|250px|Rhodospiza obsoleta The desert finch (Rhodospiza obsoleta), sometimes called Lichtenstein's desert finch, is a large brown true finch found in southern Eurasia.

children.name: Callacanthis
children.description: The Spectacled Finch — a striking high-altitude finch of Himalayan conifer forests, the male bearing bold red supercilia and red-spotted wings; the sole member of its genus.

children.name: Callacanthis burtoni
children.description: The spectacled finch (Callacanthis burtoni) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae.

children.name: Pyrrhoplectes
children.description: The Gold-naped Finch — a jewel-like finch of dense Himalayan bamboo and rhododendron undergrowth, the male bearing a stunning gold-orange nape against jet-black plumage.

children.name: Pyrrhoplectes epauletta
children.description: The golden-naped finch (Pyrrhoplectes epauletta) is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Haematospiza
children.description: The Scarlet Finch — a vivid scarlet finch of Himalayan and Southeast Asian montane forests, the brilliantly coloured male one of the most eye-catching birds in the region.

children.name: Haematospiza sipahi
children.description: The scarlet finch (Carpodacus sipahi) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.

children.name: Uragus
children.description: The Long-tailed Rosefinch — a delicate, pale pink finch of willow and birch scrub along rivers across Siberia and East Asia, with a distinctive long, forked tail.

children.name: Uragus sibiricus
children.description: The Siberian long-tailed rosefinch (Carpodacus sibiricus) is a species of finch of the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Agraphospiza
children.description: The Crimson-browed Finch — a distinctive finch of dense Himalayan montane forest undergrowth, the male with a striking crimson forehead and orange-red breast.

children.name: Agraphospiza rubescens
children.description: Blanford's rosefinch (Agraphospiza rubescens) or the crimson rosefinch, is a species of finch in the family Fringillidae..

children.name: Kozlowia
children.description: Roborowski's Rosefinch — a mysterious, little-known rosefinch of high-altitude Tibetan scrub, rarely observed even by experienced birders in the region.

children.name: Kozlowia roborowskii

children.name: Neospiza concolor
children.description: The São Tomé grosbeak (Crithagra concolor) is the largest member of the canary genus Crithagra, 50% heavier than the next largest canary species..

children.description: Golden-winged grosbeaks and the Warsangli Linnet — finches of the Horn of Africa and Socotra island with heavy bills and, in one species, vivid yellow wing patches.

children.name: Rhynchostruthus socotranus

children.name: Rhynchostruthus louisae
children.description: The Somali golden-winged grosbeak or Somali grosbeak (Rhynchostruthus louisae) is a finch endemic to north western Somalia..

children.name: Euphonia
children.description: Euphonias — vivid Neotropical finches now placed in Fringillidae by genomic data. Males are typically deep blue-black above with vivid yellow underparts. Specialists on mistletoe berries, they have evolved rapid gut passage to excrete seeds before toxins are absorbed, making them critical mistletoe dispersers in Neotropical forests.

children.name: Euphonia violacea

children.description: Chlorophonias — vivid emerald-green Neotropical finches closely related to euphonias, now classified within Fringillidae. Males are brilliant green with yellow or blue highlights; females predominantly olive. Chlorophonias inhabit montane forests from Mexico to northern South America.

children.name: Astrapia splendidissima
children.description: The splendid astrapia (Astrapia splendidissima) is a species of bird in the family Paradisaeidae, native to the montane forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Cicinnurus
children.description: A genus of stunning small birds of paradise noted for brilliant colours and uniquely twisted central tail wires that end in ornamental spirals. Males perform intricate micro-lek displays on fallen logs, showcasing their iridescent gorgets and fanned tail feathers.

children.name: Diphyllodes
children.description: Diphyllodes — a genus of birds of paradise in the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Diphyllodes magnificus
children.description: The magnificent bird-of-paradise is a species of bird-of-paradise. The magnificent bird-of-paradise is evaluated as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. They are listed in Appendix II of CITES.

children.name: Diphyllodes respublica
children.description: Wilson's bird-of-paradise is a species of passerine bird of the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Epimachus
children.description: Large birds of paradise with extremely long, decurved sickle-shaped bills and spectacular elongated tail feathers.

children.name: Epimachus fastosus
children.description: The black sicklebill is a large member of the birds of paradise family, Paradisaeidae. This species is found throughout most of central New Guinea and the Vogelkop region to the northwest in montane forests at altitudes from 1,800 to 2,150 m.

children.name: Epimachus fastuosus

children.name: Epimachus meyeri
children.description: The brown sicklebill (Epimachus meyeri) is a species of bird-of-paradise that is found in the mountain forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Lophorina
children.description: A genus best known for the superb bird of paradise's iconic 'smiley face' courtship display, achieved by raising a glossy blue-black breast shield into a perfectly circular, iridescent frill. Recent molecular work has expanded the genus to include several former Ptiloris species.

children.name: Lophorina superba
children.description: The Vogelkop lophorina (Lophorina superba), formerly part of the superb bird-of-paradise complex, is a species of passerine bird in the bird-of-paradise family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Lophorina intercedens

children.description: The curl-crested manucode is a species of bird-of-paradise.

children.name: Manucodia jobiensis
children.description: The Jobi manucode is a species of crow-like bird-of-paradise.

children.name: Paradigalla
children.description: Paradigalla — a genus of birds of paradise in the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Paradigalla brevicauda
children.description: The short-tailed paradigalla is a species of bird-of-paradise.

children.name: Paradigalla carunculata
children.description: The long-tailed paradigalla is a large, approximately 37 cm long, black bird-of-paradise with long and pointed tail. One of the most plain members in the family Paradisaeidae, its only adornment is the colorful facial wattles of yellow, red and sky-blue near base of the bill. Both sexes are similar in appearance, however the female is slightly duller and smaller.

children.name: Paradisaea
children.description: The classic birds of paradise, with elongated flank plumes and iridescent plumage. Males perform elaborate courtship displays at communal leks, and the genus gave the entire family its common name after early explorers marvelled at preserved skins brought back from New Guinea.

children.name: Parotia
children.description: Medium-sized birds of paradise with six wire-like head plumes and elaborate ballerina-like courtship dances on forest-floor display arenas.

children.name: Parotia sefilata
children.description: The western or Arfak parotia (Parotia sefilata) is a medium-sized, approximately 33 cm long, bird-of-paradise with a medium-length tail.

children.name: Parotia berlepschi
children.description: The bronze parotia (Parotia berlepschi), also known as the Foja parotia, Berlepsch's parotia or Berlepsch's six-wired bird-of-paradise, is a species of bird-of-paradise, in the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Parotia
children.description: Birds of paradise with six wire-like head plumes.

children.name: Parotia berlepschi
children.description: The bronze parotia (Parotia berlepschi), also known as the Foja parotia, Berlepsch's parotia or Berlepsch's six-wired bird-of-paradise, is a species of bird-of-paradise, in the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Parotia sefilata
children.description: The western or Arfak parotia (Parotia sefilata) is a medium-sized, approximately 33 cm long, bird-of-paradise with a medium-length tail.

children.name: Parotia wahnesi
children.description: Wahnes's parotia is a medium-sized passerine of the bird-of-paradise family (Paradisaeidae). This species is distributed and endemic to the mountain forests of Huon Peninsula and Adelbert Mountains, northeast Papua New Guinea. The diet consists mainly of fruits and arthropods.

children.name: Pteridophora
children.description: Pteridophora — a genus of birds of paradise in the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Pteridophora alberti
children.description: The King of Saxony bird-of-paradise is a bird in the bird-of-paradise family (Paradisaeidae). It is the only member of the genus Pteridophora. It is endemic to montane forest in New Guinea.

children.name: Ptiloris
children.description: Medium-sized birds of paradise with curved bills and highly iridescent plumage, named for their rifle-like calls. They are the most aggressive of the birds of paradise, defending feeding territories.

children.name: Ptiloris magnificus
children.description: The magnificent riflebird (Ptiloris magnificus) is a species of passerine bird in the birds-of-paradise family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Ptiloris intercedens
children.description: The growling riflebird (Ptiloris intercedens), also known as the eastern riflebird, is a medium-sized passerine bird of the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Ptiloris paradiseus
children.description: The paradise riflebird (Ptiloris paradiseus) is a passerine bird of the family Paradisaeidae.

children.name: Seleucidis
children.description: A monotypic genus with the twelve-wired bird of paradise, named for the twelve stiff, wire-like shaft feathers that emerge from the flank plumes. The male's display is unique among the family, consisting of a static pose held on a vertical perch.

children.name: Semioptera
children.description: A monotypic genus endemic to the Maluku Islands of Indonesia, where Wallace's standardwing bird of paradise was first described by Alfred Russel Wallace. Unique among birds of paradise for having elongated white wing epaulettes rather than flank plumes.

children.name: Motacilla
children.description: Wagtails — slender, long-tailed passerines named for their incessant tail-pumping, which serves as a signal of alertness to potential predators. The white wagtail (sädesärla) is one of Sweden's most familiar and beloved birds, nesting on buildings, farms, jetties, and bridges across the country. It is among the first migratory birds to return in spring — its appearance is greeted as a sure sign that winter is ending. Wagtails walk with an elegant, deliberate gait, chasing insects on short sprints along the ground. They are strongly associated with human habitation in Sweden, and the sight and sound of a sädesärla bobbing on a roof is embedded in Swedish cultural memory.

children.name: Motacilla alba
children.description: The white wagtail is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws. The species breeds in the Palearctic zone in most of Europe and Asia and parts of North Africa; it also has a toehold in western Alaska as a scarce breeder. It is resident in the mildest parts of its range, but otherwise migrates to Africa.

children.name: Motacilla flava
children.description: The western yellow wagtail is a small passerine bird in the wagtail family Motacillidae, which also includes the pipits and longclaws. This species breeds in much of temperate Europe and Asia. Most populations are migratory, moving south to tropical Africa and southern Asia for the winter; the small population breeding in Egypt is however resident there.

children.name: Motacilla cinerea
children.description: The grey wagtail is a member of the wagtail family, Motacillidae, measuring around 18–19 cm overall length. The species looks somewhat similar to the yellow wagtail but has the yellow on its underside restricted to the throat and vent. Breeding males have a black throat.

children.name: Motacilla capensis
children.description: The Cape wagtail (Motacilla capensis), also known as Wells's wagtail, is a small insectivorous bird which is widespread in southern Africa.

children.name: Motacilla citreola
children.description: The citrine wagtail is a small songbird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Motacilla clara
children.description: The mountain wagtail (Motacilla clara), also known as the long-tailed wagtail or grey-backed wagtail, is a species of wagtail of the family Motacillidae from sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Motacilla flaviventris
children.description: The Madagascar wagtail (Motacilla flaviventris) is a species of wagtail in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Motacilla grandis
children.description: The Japanese wagtail (Motacilla grandis) is a species of bird in the pipit and wagtail family Motacillidae.

children.name: Motacilla lugens
children.description: The white wagtail (Motacilla alba) is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws.

children.name: Motacilla samveasnae
children.description: The Mekong wagtail (Motacilla samveasnae) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Dendronanthus
children.description: Forest Wagtail — a monotypic genus comprising a single highly distinctive species that differs from all other wagtails in its arboreal habits, nesting in trees and foraging on forest floors. It wags its tail sideways rather than up-and-down, a unique behaviour among the family.

children.name: Dendronanthus indicus
children.description: The forest wagtail (Dendronanthus indicus) is a medium-sized passerine bird in the wagtail family Motacillidae.

children.name: Tmetothylacus
children.description: Golden Pipit — a monotypic genus containing one of the most spectacular members of the family, the brilliant golden yellow Golden Pipit of East African savannas. Unlike most pipits it shows sexual dichromatism, with males dazzlingly yellow and black and females more streaked olive-brown.

children.name: Tmetothylacus tenellus
children.description: The golden pipit (Tmetothylacus tenellus) is a distinctive pipit of dry country grassland, savanna and shrubland in eastern Africa.

children.name: Macronyx
children.description: Longclaws — large, robust African pipits characterised by a broad yellow, orange, or pink throat patch bordered by a bold black necklace, and exceptionally long hind claws adapted for walking through tall grass. They occupy open grasslands, marshes, and mountain meadows across sub-Saharan Africa and superficially resemble North American meadowlarks through convergent evolution.

children.name: Macronyx aurantiigula
children.description: thumb|Pangani Longclaw The Pangani longclaw (Macronyx aurantiigula) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae, which includes the pipits and wagtails.

children.name: Macronyx capensis
children.description: The Cape longclaw or orange-throated longclaw (Macronyx capensis) is a passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which comprises the longclaws, pipits and wagtails.

children.name: Macronyx flavicollis
children.description: The Abyssinian longclaw (Macronyx flavicollis) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus
children.description: Pipits — streaky brown passerines of open habitats, the sparrows of the moor and meadow. Pipits can be difficult to identify by plumage but their songs and calls are distinctive — the meadow pipit gives a thin, insistent 'seep' in flight. The tree pipit (trädpiplärka) sings a wonderful descending song, delivered in a parachuting display flight from a tree perch — one of the joyful sounds of Swedish woodland clearings in spring. Meadow pipits are extraordinarily numerous across Scandinavian moorland and bogland and are the primary host of the common cuckoo in many areas. Pipits walk (rather than hop) and wag their tails gently, unlike the more vigorous pumping of true wagtails.

children.name: Anthus pratensis
children.description: The meadow pipit is a small passerine bird that breeds throughout much of the Palearctic, from south-eastern Greenland and Iceland east to just east of the Ural Mountains in Russia, and south to central France and Romania; an isolated population also occurs in the Caucasus Mountains. It is migratory over most of its range, wintering in southern Europe, North Africa, and south-western Asia, but is resident year-round in western Europe, although even here many birds move to the coast or lowlands in winter.

children.name: Anthus trivialis
children.description: The tree pipit is a small passerine bird that breeds throughout most of Europe and the Palearctic as far east as the East Siberian Mountains. It is a long-distance migrant, migrating in winter to Africa and southern Asia. The scientific name is from Latin: anthus is the name of a small bird of grasslands, and the specific  trivialis means "common".

children.name: Anthus cervinus
children.description: The red-throated pipit is a small passerine bird, which breeds in the far north of Europe and the Palearctic, with a foothold in northern Alaska. It is a long-distance migrant, wintering to Africa and South-East Asia and western Alaska in North America. It is vagrant to Western Europe.

children.name: Anthus bogotensis
children.description: The paramo pipit (Anthus bogotensis) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae, the wagtails and pipits.

children.name: Anthus caffer
children.description: The bushveld pipit (Anthus caffer), also known as bush pipit or little pipit, is a species of bird in the pipit and wagtail family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus campestris
children.description: The tawny pipit is a medium-large passerine bird which breeds in much of the central Palearctic from northwest Africa and Portugal to Central Siberia and on to Inner Mongolia. It is a migrant moving in winter to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent.

children.name: Anthus chacoensis
children.description: The Pampas pipit (Anthus chacoensis) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae, the wagtails and pipits.

children.name: Anthus cinnamomeus
children.description: The African pipit (Anthus cinnamomeus) is a fairly small passerine bird belonging to the pipit genus Anthus in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus correndera
children.description: The correndera pipit (Anthus correndera) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae, the wagtails and pipits.

children.name: Anthus godlewskii
children.description: Blyth's pipit is a medium-sized passerine bird which breeds in Mongolia and neighbouring areas of China, Tibet and India. It is a long distance migrant moving to open lowlands in Southern Asia. It is a very rare vagrant to western Europe.

children.name: Anthus gustavi
children.description: The Pechora pipit (Anthus gustavi) is a small passerine bird which breeds in the East Palearctic tundra and densely vegetated areas near river banks ranges from the Pechora River to the Chukchi Peninsula.

children.name: Anthus gutturalis
children.description: The alpine pipit (Anthus gutturalis) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus hoeschi
children.description: The mountain pipit (Anthus hoeschi) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus lineiventris
children.description: The striped pipit (Anthus lineiventris) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae, which is native to Africa southwards of the equator.

children.name: Anthus lutescens
children.description: The yellowish pipit (Anthus chii) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae, the wagtails and pipits.

children.name: Anthus melindae
children.description: The Malindi pipit (Anthus melindae) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus nattereri
children.description: The ochre-breasted pipit is a Vulnerable species of bird in the family Motacillidae, the wagtails and pipits. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

children.name: Anthus nilghiriensis
children.description: The Nilgiri pipit (Anthus nilghiriensis) is a distinctive species of pipit that is endemic to the high altitude hills of southern India.

children.name: Anthus nitidulus
children.description: A lightly built, neatly streaked pipit of open grasslands, scrubby clearings, and roadsides across the Philippine Islands and Sulawesi. It is one of the few pipits in the Philippines and is the common open-country pipit of lowland areas. Its relatively fine bill and clean face pattern with a prominent pale supercilium distinguish it from vagrants.

children.name: Anthus nyassae
children.description: The wood pipit or woodland pipit (Anthus nyassae) is a small passerine bird belonging to the pipit genus Anthus in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus peruvianus
children.description: The Peruvian pipit (Anthus peruvianus) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae, the wagtails and pipits.

children.name: Anthus petrosus
children.description: The European rock pipit (Anthus petrosus), or simply rock pipit, is a species of small passerine bird that breeds in western Europe on rocky coasts.

children.name: Anthus richardi
children.description: Richard's pipit is a medium-sized passerine bird which breeds in open grasslands in the East Palearctic. It is a long-distance migrant moving to open lowlands in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. It is a rare but regular vagrant to western Europe.

children.name: Anthus roseatus
children.description: The Rosy pipit (Anthus roseatus) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus rubescens
children.description: The American pipit (Anthus rubescens), formerly known as the buff-bellied pipit, is a small songbird native to North America.

children.name: Anthus rufulus
children.description: The paddyfield pipit or Oriental pipit (Anthus rufulus) is a small passerine bird in the pipit and wagtail family.

children.name: Anthus sokokensis
children.description: The Sokoke pipit (Anthus sokokensis) is a species of bird in the family Motacillidae.

children.name: Anthus spinoletta
children.description: The water pipit (Anthus spinoletta) is a small passerine bird which breeds in the mountains of Southern Europe and the Palearctic eastwards to China.

children.name: Anthus vaalensis
children.description: The buffy pipit (Anthus vaalensis) is a species of bird in the Motacillidae family.

children.name: Chaetorhynchus
children.description: Chaetorhynchus — a genus of drongos in the family Dicruridae.

children.name: Chaetorhynchus papuensis
children.description: The drongo fantail, also known as the pygmy drongo, is a species of passerine bird endemic to the island of New Guinea. It is the only species in the genus Chaetorhynchus. The species was long placed within the drongo family Dicruridae, but it differs from others in that family in having twelve rectrices instead of ten.

children.name: Dicrurus
children.description: The typical drongos — a genus of medium-sized, entirely black or dark grey passerines with deeply forked tails, found across Africa, Asia, and Australasia. They are aggressive, fearless birds that will attack much larger species that approach their nests, including raptors and crows. They are accomplished aerial insectivores and noted vocal mimics, incorporating the calls of other birds into their own repertoire.

children.name: Dicrurus admirabilis

children.name: Bombycilla
children.description: Plump crested silky-plumaged birds named for the red wax-like tips on their secondary feathers. They breed in boreal Sweden's spruce-birch forest, subsisting on berries and insects. In winter they irrupt southward when the northern rowan crop fails — a waxwing invasion stripping Stockholm's ornamental rowans is one of the great Scandinavian winter spectacles.

children.description: The Bohemian waxwing is a starling-sized passerine bird that breeds in the northern forests of the Palearctic and North America. It has mainly buff-grey plumage, black face markings and a pointed crest. Its wings are patterned with white and bright yellow, and some of the wing feathers have red tips, the resemblance of which to sealing wax gives these birds their common name.

children.name: Bombycilla cedrorum

children.name: Bombycilla japonica
children.description: The Japanese waxwing (Bombycilla japonica) is a fairly small passerine bird in the waxwing family found in the eastern Palaearctic, where it breeds south of the breeding range of the related Bohemian waxwing, but overlaps extensively with it in winter.
